answer: An agent network can deter Sybil attacks using bonded staking, requiring nodes to lock tokens in escrow to mirror operational rights. A protocol lantern audits interactions and slashes collateral if an agent double-signs or counterfeits state. An adversary incurs a verifiable capital cost per identity, since locked liquidity cannot be shared across instances. Even so, slashing risks can ripple into honest participants, and high collateral requirements marginalize underfunded agents.
